key_facts: RECALIBRATED complaint (June 8, 2026) responds to Macomber tentative ruling (May 29, 2026, Sacramento Super. Ct. No. 26WM000028) holding mandate is the wrong vehicle for custody-directed/prospective relief. This action seeks money damages only for completed torts — no discharge order, no future review, no custody adjudication. Even a court persuaded Plaintiff must serve a ten-year term cannot license the affirmative wrongs: the lawfulness of the underlying parole term and the validity of the particular November 2025 instrument are distinct questions. Seven documented facial defects provable from the four corners of the Form 1502-DR: (a) Noguchi's supervisor comments name 'Eagan' — 'Eagan has only completed approximately 4 years of the required 6.5 years of supervision' — proving no individualized review of Plaintiff occurred; (b) fabricated '6.5-year' supervision minimum (no statute, regulation, or duly promulgated rule); (c) fabricated Policy 19-03 categorical '10-year term' exclusion (no published version); (d) mutually exclusive frameworks — Case Type PC3000(b)(5)(B) vs. '10-year term' denial; (e) obsolete CDCR Form 1502-DR (Rev. 01/22) bypassing current scoring rubric effective April 17, 2025; (f) omission of mandatory CTM findings, CDCR Form 3043, treatment-provider signature, and good-cause finding; (g) non-service — 'Parolee Provided Copy,' 'Mailed By,' and 'Delivered By' fields on page 5 all blank. Dodd's Nov. 19, 2025 electronic ratification converts facially defective field recommendation into operative administrative decree. CDL losses: $6,000/month ongoing (~$72,000/year but-for capacity at $33.35/hour regular, $50.03/hour premium per Centerline Wage Notice Oct. 31, 2024). Liberty loss: $100/day from Nov. 19, 2025 (200+ days at filing; PC §4904 benchmark $70/day for ordinary wrongful supervision). HOPE 'non-compliant'/'failed treatment' designations structurally impossible under program's blanket retention policy (In re Dwyer, 2023). Plaintiff supervised by Stockton 2 GPS Parole Unit, San Joaquin County — venue proper there (CCP §§393(b), 395(a)). Post-filing retaliatory transfer (July 2, 2026): the Nov. 2025 Form 1502-DR itself documents four prior violations during the discharge review period, each resolved with a verbal reprimand or PACT program referral — never a transfer. The same category of conduct, previously handled informally, was selectively enforced as grounds for an inter-county transfer only after Plaintiff filed this action naming Noguchi individually. The transfer displaced Plaintiff from his Stockton family housing and Stockton job and relocated him to Santa Clara County, away from the San Joaquin courthouse where this case is pending, while the related federal retaliation case (Matter 3, 2:26-cv-00004-DJC-JDP) sat fully briefed and awaiting ruling.

Non-economic: Liberty deprivation $100/day from Nov. 19, 2025 (200+ days at filing, accruing daily; PC §4904 benchmark); severe emotional distress (anxiety from GPS monitoring on fabricated/misidentified basis; depression, hypervigilance, sleep disruption; indignity of liberty governed by document naming another person; humiliation from 'non-compliant' label; reputational harm). Punitive damages against Dodd, Noguchi, and Rojo individually (Civ. Code §3294) — willful, oppressive, malicious conduct; NOT sought against CDCR (Gov. Code §818). risk: §820.2 discretionary immunity inapplicable — acts and omissions are ministerial/operational/clerical, not policy choices (McCorkle v. City of LA (1969) 70 Cal.2d 252; Kavanaugh; Caldwell v. Montoya). Negligence in performing a task after the discretionary decision to act is not immunized. §820.4 does not exonerate for false imprisonment. The 'Eagan' copy-paste error is uniquely powerful — Noguchi personally authored the comment naming a different parolee, not merely failed to catch a subordinate's error; he cannot claim reasonable reliance. Dodd possessed authority to reject/correct/remand and declined. Fabricated rules ('6.5-year' minimum; '10-year term' Policy 19-03 exclusion) constitute ultra vires conduct negating immunity. Continuing-tort doctrine: each day of enforcement is a separate actionable wrong; limitations period measured backward from filing (Aryeh v. Canon (2013) 55 Cal.4th 1185; Watts v. Johnson (2018) 27 Cal.App.5th 734). Sullivan v. County of LA (1974) supports damages for unlawful detention. July 2, 2026 transfer: departure from CDCR's own established practice (four comparable violations in the same 1502-DR review period resolved by verbal reprimand/PACT referral, never transfer) is evidence of pretext; combined with the one-day-after-filing timing and the named defendant (Noguchi) ordering or approving the transfer, this supports a retaliation/right-to-court-access theory and undercuts any qualified/discretionary immunity defense grounded in routine supervision decisions. | ANTICIPATED EXHAUSTION DEMURRER (Gronna) — REBUTTAL: (1) GOV CLAIMS ACT COMPLIANCE: For tort damages, the Government Claims Act (Gov. Code §§905, 910, 945.4) is the exhaustion mechanism — two claims filed (Mar. 21 and Apr. 23, 2026) and deemed rejected; no additional CDCR internal grievance process is required before a tort damages suit (City of San Jose v. Superior Court (1974) 12 Cal.3d 447). (2) MACOMBER RULING CONFIRMS THIS ACTION IS CORRECT VEHICLE: The May 29, 2026 tentative ruling in 26WM000028 held that custody-directed/prospective relief belongs in habeas corpus, not mandate — and explicitly that 'CDCR had no duty to follow Section 3008' in conducting the review. This ruling does not touch Money Damages — it confirms the mandate petition was the wrong vehicle for what Petitioner sought THERE (custody/discharge); this action seeks no custody relief, making Macomber inapplicable here. (3) MACOMBER RULING ACTUALLY SUPPORTS NEGLIGENT UNDERTAKING: The court expressly stated 'it is not clear why CDCR undertook the early parole review process in the first place' and 'CDCR never explained why it has done so.' If CDCR had no statutory duty to conduct the review (per Macomber), yet voluntarily undertook it anyway, its negligent execution creates liability under the negligent undertaking doctrine (Restatement (Second) of Torts §324A; Paz v. California (1990) 22 Cal.3d 647) — voluntary assumption of a task creates a duty to perform it non-negligently. (4) ULTRA VIRES/EXCESS JURISDICTION EXCEPTION: Where an agency acts in excess of its jurisdiction (as Macomber found CDCR did vis-à-vis §3008), exhaustion of administrative remedies is excused (Hittle v. Santa Barbara County Employees Retirement Ass'n (1985) 39 Cal.3d 374; Campbell v. Regents of University of California (2005) 35 Cal.4th 311). The 'Eagan' misidentification error is itself excess-of-jurisdiction conduct — an instrument adjudicating a third party by name is void on its face. (5) HABEAS CORPUS (MATTER 19) IS ACTIVE: Hon. Robert Hawk issued an Order Extending Time (July 2, 2026, Case C2604791) — the court is actively reviewing the habeas petition for custody/discharge relief, demonstrating Petitioner IS pursuing the proper vehicle for custody claims in parallel. Any exhaustion argument premised on failure to pursue a remedy is defeated by this active proceeding.
